audio_text.text: Presenter: Today we are talking about volunteering. Maria, you spent three months teaching in a rural school. What surprised you most?

Maria: Honestly, how little equipment the school had. We only had one set of books for thirty children. But the pupils were so eager to learn that it hardly mattered. I came home convinced that enthusiasm is more important than resources.

passages.text: Scientists studying sleep have found that teenagers need around nine hours a night, yet most get far less. Early school start times are partly to blame, because teenagers' body clocks naturally shift later. Some schools that began lessons an hour later reported better attendance and higher grades. However, critics point out that later finishes can disrupt sports and part-time jobs.
